chunks: We mentioned to him al-Kufa and what land tax had been imposed upon it, and what the members of his household had done there. So he said: 'Whoever accepted Islam voluntarily, his land was left in his possession, and one-tenth (ushr) was taken from him from what the sky and rivers watered, and half the tenth (5%) from what was irrigated by rope/bucket — this applies to what they cultivated from it. As for what they did not cultivate, the Imam takes it and leases it to those who cultivate it; and it belonged to the Muslims, and upon the lessees in their shares was the tenth and half the tenth. And there is no zakat on less than five awsuq.

As for what was taken by the sword, that is up to the Imam — he leases it as he sees fit, just as the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did at Khaybar: he contracted its black (cultivated land) and its white (palm trees), meaning its land and its palms. The people say it is not valid to contract out land and palm trees, yet the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) contracted Khaybar; and upon the contractors, besides the land contract, was the tenth and half the tenth in their shares.

He also said: The people of al-Taif accepted Islam, and the tenth and half the tenth were imposed upon them. The people of Mecca — the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) entered it by force; they were captives in his hand, and he freed them and said: Go, for you are all free (tulaqa).

key_terms.الأوساق: Awsuq — plural of wasq, a grain measure (approx. 60 sa', ~130 kg); minimum threshold for zakat
key_terms.الخراج: Kharaj — land tax imposed on non-Muslims or conquered territories
key_terms.الطلقاء: Tulaqa — 'the freed ones', the name given to Meccans liberated at the Conquest of Mecca
key_terms.العشر: Ushr — one-tenth (10%) tithe on rain-fed or river-irrigated produce
key_terms.قبالة: Qabala — agricultural lease contract; 'qabbala' means to lease/contract land
key_terms.نصف العشر: Nisf al-ushr — half the tenth (5%), applied to artificially irrigated crops

ai.seo_question: What are the rules of zakat and land tax (kharaj) for agricultural produce according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: This hadith details Imam al-Ridha's (AS) legal rulings on land tax and zakat for agricultural produce. The Imam distinguishes between lands whose inhabitants converted voluntarily — where the ushr (10% or 5% depending on irrigation) applies — and lands conquered by force, which fall under the Imam's discretionary authority to lease. The Imam cites the Prophet's precedent at Khaybar and the distinct treatment of al-Taif (voluntary conversion with tithe) and Mecca (conquest followed by manumission). This teaching clarifies the Imam's sovereign role in managing conquered land for the Muslim community's benefit.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad in Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Ahmad Bin Asheym, from Safwan Bin Yahya and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who both said, ‘We mentioned Al-Kufa to himasws and what taxation had been placed upon it, and what hisasws family members had gone to. So heasws said: ‘The one who became a Muslim voluntarily, his land was left to be in his hands, and the tenth is taken from him from what is irrigated by the sky and the rivers, and half of the tenth (5%) is taken from what was (irrigated by) the sprinkling in what they had revived from it; and whatever they did not revive from it, the Imamasws would take it and contract it with the ones who do revive it. And it was so for the Muslims and upon the vendors in their shares, the tenth and half the tenth, and there was no Zakāt regarding less than five Owsaqs.

And whatever is taken by the sword, so that is up to the Imam<sup>asws</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> would contract it with one whom he<sup>asws</sup> sees fit to, just as Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had done with Khyber. He<sup>saww</sup> contracted its black and its white, meaning its land and its palm trees, and the people were saying, ‘It is not correct to contract the land and the palm trees’; and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had contracted Khyber, and upon the contractees, besides the contract of the land, was the tenth and half the tenth in their shares.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The people of Al-Taif became Muslims, and the one-tenth and half of the one-tenth was made to be upon them, the people of Makkah, Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> entered it forcibly. Thus, they were captives in his<sup>saww</sup> hands, but he<sup>asws</sup> freed them and said: ‘Go, for you are all free!’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn ‘Ushaym from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr who has said the following: “Once we spoke to him (the Imam) about al-Kufah and of taxes levied and where his family has moved. He (the Imam) said, ‘Those who willingly accepted Islam their land was left in their hands. One out of ten is received from them for what is watered from the sky and canals. There is one out of twenty for what is watered by means of drawing water of what they have revived. What is not revived is under the authority of Imam who contracts with those who revive it. The share of the Muslims on the contractors is one out of ten or one out of twenty and Zakat is not due on what is less than twenty Awsaq.

Whatever land is taken by the sword (Armed forces), it belong to the Imam who contracts it with whomever he deems proper, just as the Messenger of Allah did with the land of Khaybar and its black and white, its land and gardens. People would say land and palm trees are not proper for contract. The Messenger of Allah contracted the land of Khaybar and the contractors were to pay one out of ten or one out of twenty.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘People of Ta’if accepted Islam and they were to pay one out of ten or one out of twenty. There is the case of people of Makkah, where the Messenger of Allah entered by force, who became his captives, he set them free. Saying, “Go, you are set free.’””
